subject: TTFT & streaming cadence follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <j.blake@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-20T14:15:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming cadence follow-up

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of the items we discussed and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key perf/streaming requirements you mentioned:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): target <= 150 ms from request receipt (99th pct) for streaming replies.
- Streaming transport: prefer SSE for simplicity, but WebSocket acceptable if we need bidirectional control messages.
- Chunk cadence: want small initial chunk within TTFT target, then subsequent chunks every ~100ms (or ~10–20 tokens per chunk) to provide progressive UI updates.
- Concurrency/throughput: peak concurrent users ~2k, average request size ~120 tokens, estimated sustained throughput ~15M tokens/day, with bursts up to 3x.
- Fallback SLO: if streaming can't meet TTFT during bursts, fallback to a lower-cost non-streaming path or reduce chunk cadence to preserve availability.

Next steps we committed to: 
1) I'll share an SLO matrix and our suggested guardrails (attached) mapping instance types to expected TTFT/throughput at 95/99 pct.
2) We can run a short perf run next week (synthetic traffic + a sample of your prompt shapes) to validate TTFT and chunk cadence.
3) Provide a small demo harness (SSE + WebSocket) you can test against — we’ll instrument first-byte timing and chunk cadence.

Action items for you: please confirm the 150 ms TTFT target and the 100 ms chunk cadence as acceptable starting points, and share any additional constraints (on TLS termination, proxying, or client-side buffering).

Attached: SLO-matrix.xlsx (performance expectations by instance type), network-diagram.png (your infra from the call).

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30-min session to walk the perf plan.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Jordan Blake <j.blake@novahealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence follow-up

Thanks Aditya — great summary. Confirming a few details from our side: 

- TTFT: 150 ms (99th) is our aspiration. We can tolerate slightly higher (up to 200 ms) on heavy burst days but would like to understand tradeoffs.
- Chunk cadence: 100 ms works if chunk sizes are small (<= ~20 tokens) and ordering is preserved. Client can do reassembly.
- Transport: SSE preferred (browser clients), but we have a small internal desktop app using WebSocket. So supporting both or a translation gateway would be ideal.
- Concurrency: 2k active concurrent requests is baseline; we expect short spikes to 6k concurrent for ~5–10 minutes during business hours.
- TLS termination: we terminate TLS at our edge (CloudFront) and will forward to Redwood over an internal TLS tunnel. We will provide IP ranges for allowlisting.

One question: how do you measure TTFT with streaming? Do you include handshake time for SSE (HTTP response headers) and TLS handshake, or just server processing time? We need the numbers to be end-to-end from client initiation at our edge.

If you can run the perf run next Wednesday (Mar 28), we’ll schedule 2 hours and provide a small set of real prompts. Also, can you include a column in the SLO matrix for 99th percentile TTFT end-to-end (including typical edge latency of ~25–35 ms)?

Cheers,
Jordan
Director of Product, NovaHealth AI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <j.blake@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence follow-up

Jordan — thanks, clear and helpful. A few clarifications and our answers to your TTFT measurement question: 

- TTFT measurement: we report TTFT end-to-end as seen by the client (first byte arrival at client listener). For our perf runs we can instrument both server-side processing time and client-observed first-byte time.
- We’ll include typical edge latency (you noted ~25–35 ms) in the SLO matrix so the numbers reflect your real-world path.
- SSE vs WebSocket: we support both. Our demo harness will present an SSE endpoint and a WebSocket endpoint. We’ll also show a lightweight translation proxy if you want to keep SSE publicly exposed and WebSocket internal.
- Chunk cadence: default suggestion is initial chunk within the 99pct TTFT window, then 70–120 ms cadence. We’ll include recommended token-batching (10–20 tokens/chunk) and an option to switch to larger, less-frequent chunks under heavy load to preserve throughput.

Perf run plan (proposed for Wed Mar 28):
- Duration: 45–60 minutes of ramped traffic plus a 15-minute sustained burst window.
- Workload shapes: baseline (2k concurrent), spike (6k for 10 minutes), and a low-latency-focused sample with small prompts.
- Metrics: client-first-byte TTFT (p95/p99), server processing time, chunk cadence distribution, throughput (tokens/sec), error rate, and tail latency.
- Deliverable: post-run SLO matrix update, a short summary PDF, and a follow-up call to align on next steps.

Nextsteps: we’ll provision a sandbox and send the test endpoints + instructions by Mon Mar 26. Can you confirm you’ll provide 3 sample prompts and the CloudFront IP ranges by Mon EOD?

—Aditya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <j.blake@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-25T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming cadence follow-up

Jordan / team — looping in a couple of operational notes from our side before the perf run: 

- Security/procurement: We’ll flag that NovaHealth has an active procurement SOW process. If the perf results look good and you want Dedicated capacity, procurement will need an expected QPS/TPS estimate for sizing.
- Instrumentation: we’ll include an endpoint emitting Server-Timing headers and a small JS snippet you can drop into your web client to measure first-byte timing from the client side.
- Attachments: SLO-matrix.xlsx is the working doc; we included a column for edge-latency-adjusted TTFT as requested.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
